But I may create a followup PR to introduce the `sample` method also to `list` namespace, that will taken an `Expr` can be evaluated to a real `column`.

issue_context.title: Support expression inside `sample` function
issue_context.body:
### Description

Recently I found myself in a situation where I needed to do this:
```py
df = df.with_columns(pl.col("SomeList").sample(pl.col("N")).alias("SomeList"))
```

Basically for each row, I wanted to replace a list in `SomeList` column to a length specified in the `N` column.

Right now, the `sample` function doesn't support expressions, one can't do it. As @MarcoGorelli said in Discord, _this may be a good feature request though, as part of the great expressification_.
comments: Yes, if expression can be supported, it will become even better. I will take a look at this   recently.
Hold on, do we support sampling of list type now or I have missed something?

you're right, it's not supported, but on Discord I'd suggested something like
```python
df.with_columns(pl.col('SomeList').list.eval(pl.element().sample(n)))
```

but - even if `sample` did support expressions - I don't think it'd work to pass `sample(pl.col('n'))` in there inside of `.list.eval` anyway?

maybe `.list.sample` is warranted then?

> `maybe .list.sample is warranted then?`

Yep, I think `.list.sample` is the right way. It is difficult to expressify the original `sample`, because it will return the same dtype as the sampled column. Changing this assumption may not be very appropriate, WDYT?

There was a similar/related query on SO recently: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77135485/

The user wanted to do a `sample()` inside `.group_by()` with a variable sample size `min(n, group_size)`

> The user wanted to do a sample() inside .group_by() with a variable sample size min(n, group_size)

Alright, perhaps this is reasonable to support `Expr` that can ultimately be resolved into a single idx value(i.e. A `Series` with a length of `1`).

review_comments: I think we should `ensure` before we cast. Saves a potentially expensive cast if there are millions of rows.
I think this still has to be done @reswqa? :eyes:
Ah, my bad. I only addressed this for `DataFrame`, but somehow forget to also modify the `function_expr` part. :)
